steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The EU began as the European Coal and Steel Community in 1951 and evolved into a political and economic union of 27 member states cooperating on trade, law, and policy. | Key Fact: The UK joined the European Communities in 1973. A 1975 referendum confirmed membership with 67% voting to stay in. Membership gave access to the single market and freedom of movement. | Key Fact: The 2016 EU referendum result: 51.9% voted Leave, 48.1% voted Remain. Turnout was 72.2%. England and Wales voted Leave; Scotland and Northern Ireland voted Remain. | Key Fact: Key Leave arguments: regaining parliamentary sovereignty (making all UK laws in the UK), controlling immigration (ending freedom of movement), making independent trade deals, and saving EU budget contributions (£17.4bn gross in 2019).
